Built for Indian kitchens

One fuel across every live-fire station

Same briquette, same burn profile, whether it is a tandoor running lunch service or a hookah counter at 1 AM. Consistent sizing means your staff stop guessing how much to load.

Tandoor

Long steady heat without flare-ups, so naan and kebabs cook on a predictable cycle. Low ash means fewer mid-service clean-outs.

4 hr burn · low spark

Sigri & live grill

Uniform cube and hexagon sizing loads evenly across the grate. No chemical accelerants, so nothing transfers to the food at the table.

0% chemicals · food-safe binder

Hookah & shisha

Clean white ash and near-zero odour, so the coal does not compete with the flavour. Cubes sized for standard shisha bowls.

Super Premium grade · ash < 10%

Hotel banquets

Volume supply on a fixed schedule so banquet teams are never rationing coal mid-event. Bulk 20 kg packs for back-of-house storage.

Scheduled monthly supply

Outdoor catering

Sealed moisture-resistant packs travel well and light reliably at open venues. Predictable burn time makes per-event planning simple.

< 5% moisture · sealed packs

Cloud kitchens

Small-footprint 5 kg packs for kitchens without warehouse space, on a top-up cycle that matches your order volume.

Why kitchens switch

Against the wood charcoal you buy today

Most Indian kitchens run on loose wood or lump charcoal bought locally. Here is the operational difference, in the terms that actually show up in your kitchen — not lab numbers.

What you notice Loose wood / lump charcoal Flareon coconut briquette
Burn time per load 1–2 hrs, uneven 4 hrs, consistent
Ash left behind High, gritty, frequent clean-out < 12%, fine white ash
Sparks & smoke Common — a risk near guests Minimal, suited to live counters
Piece sizing Irregular — staff over-load to be safe Uniform — same load every time
Chemical smell on food Possible with accelerant-treated coal None — food-grade starch binder only
Supply consistency Varies by lot and vendor Same spec every delivery, one plant
Billing Often informal / cash GST invoice, rate contract
Effective cost Lower per kg, higher per hour of service Higher per kg, lower per hour of service

How to start

Four steps, no commitment until step three

01

Free trial sample

Tell us your station type and we send a sample pack to one outlet. Free — you cover courier only.

02

Kitchen trial

Run it through a normal service week. We check back on burn time, ash volume and staff feedback.

03

Rate contract

Agree a locked rate against committed monthly volume, with GST invoicing and credit terms.

04

Scheduled supply

Fixed delivery cycle to each outlet. One point of contact for reorders, claims and changes.

India desk FAQ

Common questions from purchase teams

What is the minimum order for a single restaurant?+
[X] kg for a first order. Once on a rate contract, reorder quantity is flexible against your committed monthly volume.
Do you give credit terms?+
Yes, [Net X days] after the first [X] orders are settled on delivery. Chains and hotel groups are assessed individually.
Is this the same product you export?+
Yes — identical grades from the same production line and the same ISO 9001 certified plant in Palladam. Nothing is downgraded for the domestic market.
Can we get our own branding on the packs?+
Yes, on a rate contract above [X] kg per month. You supply artwork, we handle printing and packing.
How is it cheaper if the per-kg rate is higher?+
Because a 4-hour briquette replaces two or three loads of lump charcoal over the same service. The number your kitchen should compare is cost per hour of live fire, not cost per kg.
What if a delivery arrives damaged or short?+
Raise it with your account manager within [X] days with photographs. Verified claims are replaced on the next despatch or credited.
